key_insight: In MAPbI3 precursor environments, Ti3C2Tx MXenes are chemically stabilized by MAI but rapidly degraded by I2/polyiodides and more slowly oxidized by PbI2, with precursor order strongly affecting surface evolution.
engineering_relevance: MXene-enabled perovskite inks must be formulated and sequenced carefully to preserve flake integrity and tune interfacial chemistry for optoelectronic performance.
method: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) tracked MXene surface chemistry after exposure to individual precursor components.
Density Functional Theory (DFT) explained adsorption and oxidation mechanisms at the MXene surface.
Comparative testing isolated the roles of I2/polyiodides, PbI2, and MAI in degradation or passivation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports combined XPS and DFT evidence showing rapid oxidative dissolution from iodine species, slower PbI2-driven oxidation, and MAI-induced surface passivation.
watch_item: Precursor addition order is a critical implementation variable; changing the sequence can alter MXene stability and should be controlled carefully.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
